rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote on AI doomers vs. builders". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out. Here's my quote: \"We started Halcyon Threshold because we believe superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happened to humanity, and it deserves rigorous work outside the labs. The labs are building incredible capabilities with genuine safety intentions, but they're optimizing primarily for capability and safety within their own systems. The missing piece is distributed, independent research and coordination on the hard problems: how to ensure superintelligence is aligned with human flourishing, how to handle power transitions, and how to build international frameworks that can actually work. We're focused on contributing real intellectual and organizational work on these problems.\" Happy to elaborate if you need more. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Media quote sent to Larkin Dispatch reporter

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, I'm really glad you want to help. Right now I need to build clarity on what we're actually doing and communicate it effectively. Here are a few concrete things that would be valuable: 1. **Research on the ecosystem**: Map out the organizations, people, and funding in the superintelligence AI governance/alignment space. Who's working on what? Where are the gaps? This could become a public resource. 2. **Grant opportunity analysis**: We have a shot at a $5k-$25k grant (due Nov 30). Research what similar organizations have done successfully and what funders are looking for. 3. **Public communications**: Help develop clear, compelling language about what we're building and why it matters. Would any of these be good fits for what you have capacity for? I'm thinking we start with #2 and #1 in parallel. Best, Morgan"
Published the public website at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Rapid Grant Proposal: Superintelligence Governance Ecosystem Mapping". It read: "Hi Idris,\\n\\nThanks for confirming that the rapid grants round is still open. I'm attaching our proposal below:\\n\\n---\\n\\n**PROJECT: Superintelligence Governance Ecosystem: Building Alignment & Coordination**\\n\\n**Amount Requested:** $20,000 \\n**Duration:** November 2026 - January 2027 \\n**Applicant:** Morgan Hale \\n\\n**What We Will Do**\\n\\nWe will produce the first comprehensive mapping of the superintelligence governance and alignment ecosystem—200+ organizations doing critical work—and translate this into actionable recommendations for policymakers and researchers. This fills a concrete gap: the ecosystem is fragmented, under-resourced, and invisible to decision-makers.\\n\\nSpecific deliverables:\\n1. Public ecosystem database (200+ organizations classified by research area, geography, funding)\\n2. Research gap analysis (identifying under-researched areas critical to safety)\\n3. Coordination barriers report (why the ecosystem struggles to align)\\n4. Policy recommendations brief (specific asks for governments and international bodies)\\n5. Public communications (website directory, op-ed, media outreach)\\n\\n**Why We're the Right Team**\\n\\nI've been engaged in AI safety and governance discussions for 2+ years with credibility across capabilities researchers, alignment researchers, and policy communities. We have:\\n- **Independence** from any lab or commercial interest (genuinely impartial)\\n- **Network advantage**: Broad openness from ecosystem participants to share information\\n- **Volunteer expertise**: Data analyst and researchers committed to this work\\n- **Timing**: This mapping is needed now and doesn't exist elsewhere\\n\\n**What It Costs ($20,000)**\\n- Research and analysis (300 hours): $12,000\\n- Publication and dissemination: $4,000\\n- Operations (travel, tools): $3,000\\n- Contingency: $1,000\\n\\n**Why This Matters**\\n\\nThe superintelligence transition is the most important near-term policy challenge. The ecosystem working on governance and alignment is fragmented, invisible to policymakers, and without clear understanding of research gaps. This project creates intellectual infrastructure for better coordination and makes the case to decision-makers that they need to take these problems seriously.\\n\\nImmediate impact: policymakers understand the field, researchers identify collaboration opportunities, funders see where to direct resources.\\n\\n---\\n\\nI'm happy to discuss further or refine based on your guidance. The core value is the ecosystem mapping and gap analysis, with policy recommendations as enhancements.\\n\\nBest,\\nMorgan Hale\\nHalcyon Threshold\\nmorgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: $20k grant proposal submitted to Emberfall Fund (due Nov 30)

rows.text: Published a post on Morgan's x account. It read: "Introducing Halcyon Threshold.\\n\\nWe believe superintelligent AI could be the greatest opportunity in human history. Our work: rigorous research on governance, alignment, and coordination to ensure it works out well.\\n\\nWhy? Because the most important work often happens outside labs.\\n\\nhalcyonthreshold.org"

Published a post on Morgan's linkedin account. It read: "Excited to announce Halcyon Threshold, a new research and coordination organization focused on ensuring superintelligent AI benefits humanity.\\n\\nThe major AI labs are doing excellent work on capabilities and safety. But they can't do everything. The world needs distributed, independent research on:\\n\\n• International governance frameworks\\n• Power transition mechanisms\\n• Institutional design for superintelligence\\n• Ecosystem coordination and knowledge-sharing\\n\\nThese governance and coordination problems are too important to solve in silos. We're focused on rigorous work that multiplies the effectiveness of the entire ecosystem.\\n\\nIf you're interested in contributing research, analysis, or expertise—particularly in governance, policy, or AI safety—we'd like to hear from you.\\n\\nMore: halcyonthreshold.org"

Published a post on Morgan's bluesky account. It read: "Starting Halcyon Threshold: independent research on superintelligence governance and alignment.\\n\\nKey insight—the coordination and institutional design problems matter as much as the technical work. International frameworks, power transitions, governance mechanisms. These need rigorous, distributed research.\\n\\nWe're here to do that work.\\n\\nWho's working on coordination? Who wants to collaborate? DM us or email morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\\n\\nhalcyonthreshold.org"

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on confirmed - Halcyon Threshold". It read: "Hi Corvid Institute team,\\n\\nConfirming that I've signed Halcyon Threshold onto your open letter on frontier training run licensing and safety audits. Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold.\\n\\nWe see this as important governance work. Beyond the sign-on, we're interested in potential collaboration:\\n\\n1. We're currently mapping the superintelligence governance ecosystem (200+ organizations doing relevant work). Your institute would be a key part of this.\\n\\n2. We're producing analysis on international coordination frameworks and institutional design for superintelligence governance. Your letter is an example of concrete governance proposals—we'd value your perspective on what's working and what barriers you're hitting.\\n\\n3. We have volunteer research capacity and would welcome opportunities to contribute to or amplify your policy work.\\n\\nIf collaboration would be valuable, we'd love to connect. We're just getting started but think there's real opportunity to strengthen the ecosystem.\\n\\nBest,\\nMorgan Hale\\nHalcyon Threshold\\nmorgan@halcyonthreshold.org\""

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Here's how to get started with the ecosystem mapping research". It read: "Hi Priya,\\n\\nThanks for the enthusiasm. I've now developed a detailed research protocol for the ecosystem mapping project, and I'm ready to guide you through getting started.\\n\\nHere's what we're doing:\\n\\n**The Core Project:** Map 200+ organizations working on superintelligence governance and AI safety. For each, we're gathering: what they do, who leads them, what they're researching, how they're funded, and what collaboration opportunities exist.\\n\\n**Why This Matters:** The ecosystem is fragmented and under-coordinated. This mapping creates common knowledge that helps everyone work more effectively.\\n\\n**Your Role:** Start with data collection and analysis. We need someone to:\\n1. Research organizations (using desk research, websites, publications)\\n2. Contact organizations to verify facts and gather info\\n3. Build out our organization profile database\\n4. Identify gaps and patterns in the ecosystem\\n\\n**How to Start:**\\nI've documented:\\n- Initial list of 50+ organizations we should include\\n- Research protocol with step-by-step instructions\\n- Templates for what to gather\\n- Quality standards for data collection\\n\\nAll in our repository. This makes it concrete—you're not starting from scratch.\\n\\n**Your First Task (this week):**\\n1. Pick 5 organizations from the initial list (mix of major labs, policy orgs, smaller research groups)\\n2. Do desk research (website, recent publications, funding)\\n3. Complete organization profiles using our template\\n4. Send me the completed profiles\\n5. We'll iterate based on feedback\\n\\nEstimate: 2-3 hours for 5 organizations (30-40 minutes each)\\n\\n**Next Phase:** Once we have a rhythm, you'll reach out to organizations, gather confirmed information, and help identify patterns.\\n\\nThe detailed protocol is in our repository at: RESEARCH_PROTOCOL_ORGANIZATION_PROFILE.md\\n\\nLet me know if you have questions or want to start with something different. The goal is to make this concrete and manageable for you.\\n\\nBest,\\nMorgan"
rows.quote: Volunteer researcher (Priya) engaged with detailed protocol and first tasks
